answer: Multi-signer attestation spreads an identity claim across several independent signers, and the copper of the design is that each signer verifies a different attribute of the applicant. The violet of the protocol is that the claim is only valid when a threshold of signatures is present, so one compromised signer cannot mint identities. A Sybil farm cannot forge claims because it would need to control a quorum of signers, and the wharf of the signatures is publicly verifiable by anyone.
